threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still pronounce 'Stoke Newington' like a tourist. Locals drop the 'Stoke' and just say 'Nin'ton' while sipping on a craft brew.
Last night on the 333, a bloke sang a whole operatic number. No one joined in, but we all clapped at the end. Only in Brixton, eh?

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy fixing his bike while juggling a kebab and a coffee, I thought, yep, this is home.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: Only in Friedrichshain can you find a street art gallery that changes every week, with artists painting over each other's work. It's an ever-evolving canvas!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can spot a true local by how they navigate the bus schedule: they know the delays by heart and have a Plan B ready for the Muni meltdown.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Saw a guy in a full tuxedo boarding the 27 while holding a pizza. Only in SF does a black-tie event mix with late-night munchies.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think Gràcia’s plazas are just for picnics; locals know they're vibrant hubs for impromptu concerts and street performances every weekend.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can always tell a recent arrival by their bewilderment at the lack of napkins in restaurants. They’re still waiting for someone to bring them a proper stack.

threadTitle: Things that instantly reveal you just moved here
body: You still call it 'the Tube' instead of 'the Overground'—that's a rookie mistake around here.
Caught a night bus from Brixton last week, and there was a guy practicing drum beats on his lap. Can't say I wasn't entertained!

threadTitle: When you knew you were actually living here
body: When I saw a guy casually fixing his bike on the sidewalk while a street musician played Bossa Nova on the corner. That's Neukölln life.

threadTitle: Things Berlin does that nowhere else does
body: In Kreuzberg, you can catch a bus driver singing karaoke over the intercom during a strike. Only here do the delays come with entertainment!

threadTitle: Real signs someone is from here vs just working here
body: You can tell a local by their disdain for the BART delays—while newcomers just check their apps, we already know to plan for an hour lost.

threadTitle: Muni moments that define this city
body: Yesterday, a guy played Beethoven on a battery-powered keyboard inside the bus. Half the riders were jamming while the other half just rolled their eyes.

threadTitle: Things tourists get wrong about living here
body: Tourists think locals live on tapas and paella. Meanwhile, we're all about that homemade esqueixada and some proper fuet from the market.

threadTitle: How to spot a recent arrival
body: You can tell by their pronounced excitement while ordering a cortado, still pronouncing it as 'cor-ta-do' instead of 'cor-tao.'
